candidates.name: Dr. Elena Rostova
candidates.summary: Distributed systems veteran with deep expertise in Raft consensus, eBPF telemetry, and high-throughput streaming pipelines. Proven track record scaling tier-0 infrastructure to 2M QPS across 4 regions with 99.999% uptime.

highlights: Spearheaded redesign of cross-datacenter event mesh, reducing tail P99 latency from 140ms to 18ms across 350+ nodes.
Invented dynamic quorum failover protocol for metadata registry, yielding 0 data loss during major multi-AZ outages.
Mentored 14 senior engineers across distributed storage and networking pods.
Built high-performance tiered cache engine reducing Amazon S3 egress cost by $1.8M annually.
Authored internal RFC standards for multi-tenant isolation and CPU throttling using Linux cgroups v2.

education.degree: B.S. in Electrical Engineering & Computer Science

claims.claim: Reduced P99 event ingestion latency from 140ms to 18ms at Apex Cloud
claims.evidenceSource: Apex Cloud Tech Blog post (2023) co-authored by candidate + verified GitHub PR benchmarks
claims.analysisNotes: Claims strongly substantiated by published latency benchmark telemetry and open-source contributions.
claims.followUpQuestion: Can you describe the CPU cache-line alignment optimizations applied during the batch parsing step?

claims.claim: Designed and deployed custom Raft implementation supporting 10,000 req/sec state transitions
claims.evidenceSource: USENIX ATC paper proceedings (2022) with candidate as first author
claims.analysisNotes: Direct peer-reviewed publication matches the architecture claims precisely.
claims.followUpQuestion: How did your Raft implementation handle network partitioning during leader election split-votes?

claims.claim: Led and directly managed a team of 25 distributed systems engineers
claims.evidenceSource: Reference check & LinkedIn org hierarchy cross-validation
claims.analysisNotes: Candidate acted as technical lead/architect for 14 engineers across 3 squads, but did not have direct HR/people management line responsibility for 25.
claims.followUpQuestion: In your role as tech lead, what was the boundary between your architectural ownership and the engineering manager’s headcount/performance management responsibilities?

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design a distributed lease manager that guarantees linearizable reads across 5 geographic regions with variable WAN jitter?
interviewQuestions.context: Probing candidate’s real-world boundary handling of clock drift and asymmetric network partitions.

evaluationRubric.poor: Mentions basic Redis locks without considering split-brain or network partitions.
evaluationRubric.good: Explains TrueTime/hybrid logical clocks or leader leases with synchronized duration bounds.
evaluationRubric.exceptional: Discusses exact bounds of Paxos/Raft leader lease invariants, monotonic clock drift tolerance, and read-index optimization to bypass log replication.

interviewQuestions.question: Walk us through an incident where you diagnosed an unexpected tail latency spike in Go or Rust caused by memory allocator contention or GC pause.
interviewQuestions.context: Validating claim of sub-20ms P99 latency under heavy concurrent throughput.

evaluationRubric.poor: Vague discussion of adding more CPU or using pprof without root cause analysis.
evaluationRubric.good: Describes flame graphs, memory allocation escapes to heap, or lock contention in mutexes.
evaluationRubric.exceptional: Explains specific Linux perf / eBPF tracepoints, cache thrashing, sync.Pool optimization, or bypassing GC with off-heap arenas.

interviewQuestions.question: When multiple senior engineers disagree on a critical architectural migration (e.g. gRPC vs Async Messaging), how do you drive consensus without stalling momentum?
interviewQuestions.context: Probing candidate’s leadership calibration after finding that direct reports were 14 rather than 25.

evaluationRubric.poor: Forces decision top-down or leaves team in analysis paralysis.
evaluationRubric.good: Uses RFC process, creates POC benchmarks, and defines measurable decision criteria.
evaluationRubric.exceptional: Establishes clear two-way door vs one-way door frameworks, decouples interfaces to allow parallel evolution, and runs blameless post-mortems.

keyStrengths: World-class depth in distributed state machines and consensus algorithms (Ph.D. + USENIX author).
Hands-on systems programming in Rust and Go with real production telemetry at scale.
High intellectual rigor with clear written RFC communication standards.
potentialRisks: Exaggerated people management numbers on resume; better suited for Individual Contributor Principal/Staff Architect path rather than Engineering Director.
High salary expectation ($255k base + equity) requiring executive calibration.

candidates.summary: Infrastructure leader specialized in Kubernetes cluster fleet management, GitOps deployment automation (ArgoCD), and multi-cloud cost reduction. Proven operational mastery during peak live events.

highlights: Managed 80+ multi-tenant EKS clusters running 14,000 microservice pods.
Reduced annual AWS cloud infrastructure spend by 32% ($3.2M) through Spot instance orchestration and Karpenter scaling.
Maintained 99.99% availability during live streaming of high-concurrency sporting events (8M concurrent viewers).

candidates.name: Aria Chen
candidates.summary: Pioneering AI systems engineer specializing in high-throughput LLM serving, speculative decoding, and custom Triton/CUDA kernel optimization. Co-author of prominent papers on KV-cache compression.

highlights: Built distributed LLM inference cluster serving 70B parameter models at 120 tokens/sec per GPU with 4-bit AWQ quantization.
Designed custom Triton kernel for continuous batching and cross-attention memory pooling, cutting TTFT by 45%.

claims.claim: Authored custom Triton kernels delivering 45% reduction in Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) for 70B models
claims.evidenceSource: NeurIPS 2024 Workshop paper and reproducible open-source benchmarks
claims.analysisNotes: Fully verified with code repositories and independently benchmarked speedups.
claims.followUpQuestion: How did you handle SRAM bank conflicts in the shared memory tiling strategy?

competencies.rationale: Top 1% domain authority in vLLM, TensorRT, and Triton kernel design.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain how FlashAttention-3 leverages Hopper TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) and warp group asynchronous copies to achieve near-theoretical FLOPs utilization.

evaluationRubric.poor: Mentions basic attention mechanism without hardware memory hierarchy details.
evaluationRubric.good: Explains SRAM vs HBM bandwidth bottlenecks and how tiling avoids full matrix writes.
evaluationRubric.exceptional: Breaks down Hopper async transaction barriers, TMA multicast, FP8 tensor core matrix layout, and ping-pong software pipelining.

keyStrengths: Exceptional world-class expertise in modern LLM inference systems, custom CUDA/Triton kernels, and hardware utilization.
Strong research background with immediate practical production deployment skills.
potentialRisks: High demand candidate with competing offers from top frontier labs.
